name: Harakmbut, Amarakaeri/Arakmbut variety
confidence_why: Three first-hand sources agree that Amarakaeri stress is penultimate, but only Van linden 2023, with transcribed examples of case-marked nouns, works out the domain (root plus derivational affixes, inflectional suffixes excluded), while the brief orthographic notes of Tripp 1995 ("generalmente la penúltima sílaba") and Helberg 1996 ("regularmente en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra") state plain word-penultimate stress without examining inflected words.

catalog_quote: The domain of stress assignment in a phonological word differs according to word class. For nouns, the stress domain is the root plus derivational affixes; the main stress falls on the penultimate syllable. In examples (1)–(5), word stress has been indicated through the stress symbol [ˈ] or underlined syllable nuclei. As shown in (3) and (5c), inflectional suffixes like case endings do not bear on stress assignment. By contrast, derivational suffixes attaching to nouns typically affect stress placement (5). (5) a. wã-wẽ [ˈwã.wɛ̃] NMLZ-liquid ‘liquid, river’ b. wã-wẽ-ẽrĩ [wã.ˈwɛ̃.rĩ] NMLZ-liquid-AN ‘river spirit’ c. wã-wẽ-ẽrĩ-tã [wã.ˈwɛ̃.rĩ.tã] NMLZ-liquid-AN-ACC ‘river spirit’ (direct object function) Verb forms also show stress on the penultimate syllable, but they have a different stress domain, as not all derivational suffixes are included (e.g., the transitivizer -a in (6) does not …

new_statements.quote: Las normas de acentuación del idioma amarakaeri son simples: generalmente la penúltima sílaba lleva el acento. Como la acentuación es, en general, predecible no se marca en las palabras.
new_statements.translation: The accentuation rules of the Amarakaeri language are simple: generally the penultimate syllable carries the stress. Since accentuation is, in general, predictable, it is not marked on words.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; because it is predictable it is left unmarked in the orthography (the hedge 'generalmente' admits unspecified exceptions).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the opened pages.
new_statements.exceptions: None specified; the statement is hedged with 'generalmente' / 'en general', implying some exceptions exist but none are listed. The dictionary describes the Puerto Luz variety (Prólogo, p. 9).
new_statements.identity_note: Tripp 1995 describes the Puerto Luz variety of Amarakaeri (Prólogo, p. 9: 'Este diccionario muestra la variedad de Puerto Luz, un pueblo situado a orillas del río Colorado'), one of five village varieties; the Toyeri and Sapiteri dialects are referred to Peck 1979. Helberg 1996 labels the language 'Harakmbut' generally; Van linden's data are Arakmbut/Amarakaeri.

sources.citation: Helberg Chávez, Heinrich Albert. 1996. Mbaisik: En la penumbra del atardecer. Literatura oral del pueblo harakmbut. Lima: CAAAP. [Rosetta Project excerpt: 'Indicaciones sobre el Alfabeto', 3 pp.]
sources.quote: 'El acento recae regularmente en la penúltima sílaba de la palabra, y va acompañado de elevación de tono. — En verbos complejos hay un acento secundario sobre la penúltima sílaba de la raíz verbal. Esto es válido también para sustantivos y verbos compuestos.' (primary stress = word-penult with pitch rise; morphology conditions only a SECONDARY stress on the root penult).
